$comment: TASK-970 — the reasoning-posture cross-language contract fixture. Authored by the orchestrator BEFORE the implementation lanes, so `packages/applications` (producer) and `apps/text` (consumer) build against one written shape instead of discovering it mid-flight. `wire` is what @arcaai/applications MUST send on GenerateRequest; `support` is what each adapter MUST declare about its own engine. OWNERSHIP: the Python lane (L1) is the ONLY writer of `support[*].renders` and `support[*].class` — it must VERIFY each against the deployed engine version and correct this file where the seeded guess is wrong. Every other lane reads it. The seeded values below are a STARTING POINT taken from documentation knowledge with a May-2026 cutoff; they are explicitly NOT authoritative and a lane that ships them unverified has not done the work.
why: Before TASK-970 the posture was pre-rendered TS-side into `extra.reasoning_effort` (agent-reasoning.ts::reasoningExtra maps `enabled:false` -> 'minimal'). That is LOSSY: once on the wire, 'minimal' cannot be distinguished from an admin who asked for minimal EFFORT, and an engine with a true off-switch (Ollama `think:false`) can no longer be driven correctly. The posture therefore travels as a posture and each adapter renders it.

cases.name: off
cases.meaning: Admin turned reasoning OFF on the agent. Render the engine's own off-switch.

cases.name: on-unspecified
cases.meaning: Reasoning on, no budget named. Render 'on' without pinning an effort.

cases.name: on-effort
cases.meaning: Reasoning on at a named budget. Effort vocabulary: minimal|low|medium|high.

cases.name: absent
cases.meaning: No posture at any tier. Send NOTHING; the engine decides. Never synthesize a default here — the platform tier (text.reasoning.defaultEffort) already resolved before the wire.

wire.caller_override: `extra.reasoning_effort` REMAINS supported and still wins per-key, preserving the documented 'CALLER WINS, per key' rule in TextRequestEnrichmentService. A call site that pins the raw ride-along is not second-guessed.

support.$comment: VERIFIED by the L1 (adapters) lane on 2026-09-13 against the client library each adapter actually pins (apps/text/pyproject.toml, resolved in conda env `arcaenv`) and, for the HTTP engines that pin no client, against the deployed image and the engine's own documentation. Two seeded guesses were WRONG and are corrected here: `openai`/`azure_openai` were seeded `effort-only` but the pinned SDK's own `ReasoningEffort` literal carries a true `"none"` rung, and `vertex` was seeded `unsupported` but the pinned SDK exposes a full off-switch AND an effort dial. `class`/`renders` describe WHAT THE ADAPTER RENDERS, not merely what the vendor could theoretically accept: where a vendor parameter exists but cannot be driven safely for every model of that engine, the adapter does not send it and records the posture as unenforceable instead (owner decision: log and proceed, never fail the call).

$classes.native-off: the engine has a TRUE off-switch this adapter renders; `effort` says whether it also has a dial the adapter can drive
$classes.effort-only: an effort can be expressed but OFF cannot; `enabled: false` is RECORDED as unenforceable, never approximated onto a low effort — that lossy mapping is the defect this contract removes
$classes.unsupported: the transport cannot express the posture at all -> log and proceed

$fields.renders: the engine parameter the OFF/ON posture is rendered into; null when nothing is sent
$fields.effort: the engine parameter a named effort is rendered into; null when the adapter cannot pin a budget, in which case ON is still rendered and the EFFORT is recorded as unenforceable
$fields.verified: true only when checked against a pinned artifact or the engine's own documentation, with the check named in `evidence`

openai.evidence: openai==3.1.0 (pinned `openai>=3.1.0,<4`): `openai/types/shared/reasoning_effort.py` declares `ReasoningEffort = Optional[Literal['none','minimal','low','medium','high','xhigh','max']]`, and `chat/completion_create_params.py` carries `reasoning_effort: Optional[ReasoningEffort]`. `'none'` is the off-switch; minimal|low|medium|high are all legal rungs.

azure_openai.evidence: Same pinned SDK and the same `chat.completions.create` wire (AsyncAzureOpenAI). The api-version the adapter is written against is `2024-12-01-preview` (AzureOpenAIProvider.ADAPTER_API_VERSION); a connection may pin a newer one.

openai_compat.evidence: NOT VERIFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION — this adapter is 'any server that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions wire' and is documented as wire-only (`providers/openai_compat.py` docstring). An effort rung is standard OpenAI vocabulary and is passed through; `'none'` is a newer rung this adapter cannot promise an unknown server understands, and an unknown enum value is a 400 the owner decision rules out — so OFF is recorded, not guessed.

lmstudio.evidence: LM Studio's OpenAI-compatibility docs and its API changelog document `reasoning_effort` with the rungs low|medium|high (gpt-oss); no off value is documented on /v1/chat/completions. Deployed as the in-cluster `hope-lmstudio` image (deployment repo `base/lmstudio.yaml`).

vllm.evidence: Deployed image `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0` (deployment repo `base/vllm.yaml:88`) serving a Qwen3-class checkpoint (`base/config/vllm.env`). vLLM's own reasoning-outputs docs give `extra_body={'chat_template_kwargs': {'enable_thinking': False}}` as the per-request off-switch for that family. There is no effort dial on that toggle, so a named effort is recorded as unenforceable.

ollama.evidence: Ollama's Thinking docs (docs.ollama.com/capabilities/thinking): `think` on /api/generate takes true|false, and SOME models additionally take the levels low|medium|high|max. Booleans are universal, the levels are per-model, so this adapter renders only the boolean and records a named effort as unenforceable — sending a level to a boolean-only model would fail the call. NOTE: before this ticket the adapter sent a hardcoded `think: true` on EVERY request; that literal is gone.

anthropic.evidence: anthropic==0.122.0 (pinned `anthropic>=0.122.0`): `message_create_params.thinking: ThinkingConfigParam` = Union[Enabled, Disabled, Adaptive]. OFF is `{'type': 'disabled'}`; ON with no named budget is `{'type': 'adaptive'}` (the engine picks). The only budget the vendor accepts is `budget_tokens: int` (required, >= 1024) — a token COUNT, not an effort rung, so this adapter will not invent one and records a named effort as unenforceable.

vertex.evidence: google-genai==2.18.1 (pinned `google-genai>=2.18.1`): `types.GenerateContentConfig.thinking_config: ThinkingConfig`, whose `thinking_budget` is documented '0 is DISABLED, -1 is AUTOMATIC', and whose `thinking_level: ThinkingLevel` enumerates MINIMAL|LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH — an exact match for this contract's effort vocabulary. The seeded `unsupported` was wrong.

llama_cpp.evidence: This adapter targets llama.cpp's NATIVE `/completion` endpoint (providers/llama_cpp.py), deliberately, for its `timings` block. llama.cpp's server README documents `reasoning_effort`, `reasoning_format`, `reasoning_control` and `chat_template_kwargs` on `/v1/chat/completions` ONLY; `/completion` is a raw-prompt endpoint that applies no chat template and accepts no reasoning parameter. `--reasoning-budget` is a server CLI flag, not per-request.

bedrock.evidence: botocore==1.43.72 service model `bedrock-runtime/2023-09-30`: `ConverseRequest` has no reasoning member; the only route is `additionalModelRequestFields`, a free-form `Document` passed through to the UNDERLYING model's own vocabulary. That vocabulary differs by model family and generation (`reasoning_config` for Claude 3.7, `thinking` for Sonnet 4 / adaptive on Opus) and a key the family does not know is a ValidationException — i.e. a failed generation, which the owner decision forbids. A normalized posture therefore cannot be rendered here until the bound model declares its own family vocabulary (WS-3 territory).

unenforceable.owner_decision: 2026-09-13 — an engine that cannot honour the posture sends nothing, records provider + model + posture on the generation's telemetry, and the call RUNS. No 422: a tuning knob must not become an outage risk on a provider swap.
unenforceable.must_not: Silently drop. Today's defect is that seven adapters drop the posture with no record at all.
